designs.title: Vitis vinifera
designs.why: Strong diagonal from the branch, a clear focal mass in the grape cluster, and a varied, confident line that holds up at full size. The captions are set in a fitting old-style serif with an italic binomial, which feels right for a plate. The weak points are that the pruned cane floats high on the right with a dead quadrant below it, and the captions sit loose with no leader lines, so 'Grapes (fruit)' reads as an orphan in the gap at lower centre.
designs.fix: Rebalance the right column: drop the pruned cane so it sits lower and aligns with the cluster (or move its caption to the bottom margin), then set all three captions on one shared baseline grid so they read as a deliberate system.

designs.title: Fermentation
designs.why: Best-organised sheet of the three. The tall vessel anchors a strong vertical. The magnified yeast roundel gives a secondary focal point and fills the right-hand negative space. Labels are set in one consistent serif with proper subscript CO2, and leader arrows are clean, so it reads like a real technical plate. White ink on black works well because the dense wort texture glows. In the full-size crops, the 'Budding yeast cell' leader forks into two lines, and one ends in stray specks. There is also a loose tick mark left of the roundel. The 'Yeast Activity (magnified)' heading is bold while every other label is regular, which jumps the hierarchy.
designs.fix: Clean up the label layer: give each label a single leader, remove the stray marks near the roundel, and set the roundel heading in the same weight as the other labels (small caps or letterspaced) so the label system is uniform.

designs.title: Shaping
designs.why: The figure has energy, and the white foam blank makes a good bright ellipse at centre. But the drawing is a near-rectangular slab of heavy, broken scratch texture cut off flat at the bottom, so it reads as a scanned photo block rather than a shaped T-shirt graphic. Up close, the sawdust and shelf areas break up into noisy, mottled marks. The heading is a generic, widely tracked geometric sans with a thin rule. It has no relationship to the gritty illustration and looks pasted on, too small and too timid for the image beneath it.
designs.fix: Give the image a designed silhouette (vignette or fade out the shelf and legs instead of a hard bottom crop) and redraw the heading so it belongs to the illustration: a heavier condensed or hand-cut letterform sized to the full blank width, locked closer to the head.
